RJML Labs · Experiment

Flow around objects

A real flow solver running in your browser. It solves the 2D Navier–Stokes equations with the lattice Boltzmann method, so the pressure, vortices and wake you see are computed, not drawn. Change the shape, fluid, speed and angle and watch the forces respond.

What is being computed

The solver uses a D2Q9 lattice Boltzmann scheme on a 360 × 170 grid. Fluid enters from the left at a fixed speed and leaves on the right, and the top and bottom edges are slip walls. The object is a no-slip wall, and the force on it is measured by momentum exchange at the surface, then turned into Cd and Cl using the chord, side or diameter as the reference length (0.1 m).

Air versus water

The flow depends on the Reynolds number, Re = ρUL/μ, not on speed alone. At the same speed, water gives a Reynolds number about 55 times higher than air. Tick “Keep Reynolds number when changing medium” and switch between them: the speed changes but the flow pattern does not.

Limits of this model

This is a numerical simulation result and an educational model. It is two-dimensional, so it cannot show real three-dimensional turbulence. A browser grid can only resolve a limited Reynolds number, so above the cap shown in the banner the solver runs at the cap and adds a Smagorinsky sub-grid viscosity to stay stable; the physical value is still reported. Blockage from the nearby slip walls raises the drag a little. Results depend on mesh resolution, boundary conditions and the turbulence model, and this result has not necessarily been experimentally validated.
